title: Work stress, burn-out and return to work
summary: For long-term work stress and burn-out (an occupational phenomenon in ICD-11, not a mental disorder) and for planning a graded return to work after health-related leave. Screen first for conditions that need their own plan.

problems.label: Exhaustion and distance from work after long-term work stress
definitions: Feels drained most of the time, more cynical or detached about work, and less effective, and links this to ongoing work demands.
Works long or unpredictable hours, takes little leave, or has high demands with little control or support.
longTermGoals: The client recovers energy, has clearer limits around work, and any condition that needs its own plan is identified and addressed.

shortTermObjectives.text: At intake, screen for depression, anxiety and sleep problems with the PHQ-9, the GAD-7 and a sleep review, and add or switch to the matching plan library if one fits, since burn-out is a work-related state rather than a mental disorder.
By session 3, map work demands, control, support, reward and fairness with the client, and choose 1 or 2 areas where change is within reach.

Over weeks 3 to 8, keep at least 2 limits on work time (for example a fixed finish time, or no work messages after a set hour) on at least 4 days a week, and rate energy (0-10) at the end of each week.
By week 4, schedule at least 3 recovery activities a week outside work (rest, movement, time with people or hobbies) and track them.
Over weeks 3 to 10, learn and use at least 1 stress-management skill (for example applied relaxation or structured problem solving) during work stress at least 3 times a week.

zCodes.label: Other physical and mental strain related to work

problems.label: Time off work for health reasons, with a planned return
definitions: Is on sick leave or reduced duties because of mental health and is unsure how or when to return.
Worries about how colleagues or managers will react, or whether the job can be adjusted.
longTermGoals: The client returns to work, or to another valued role, in a planned, graded way with any adjustments they need.

shortTermObjectives.text: By week 2, agree with the client how and when they want to keep in touch with the workplace during leave, and who the contact person will be.
By week 4, write a graded return plan with the client (for example reduced hours or duties rising over 4 to 8 weeks), to share with the employer or occupational health only with the client's consent.

Before the return date, decide with the client whether to ask for workplace adjustments (for example a changed schedule, a quieter space or extra breaks) and, if they ask, provide a brief letter that describes functional needs without diagnosis details (the accommodation letter tool can help).
During the first 4 weeks back, review progress every 1 to 2 weeks and adjust the plan if symptoms come back.
